added_claims.speaker: Nick Balters
added_claims.quote: part of the reason why you see less on the fixed income and effects side is that historically liquidity has improved
added_claims.claim: Fixed income and FX are a small part of QIS because banks' QIS business grew out of equity long/short, commodity roll indices and delta-1 products, and academic risk-premia work has been mostly on equities; Nick sees fixed income and FX as now in a growth phase.
added_claims.direction: growth in rates and FX risk-premia indices

added_claims.claim: The $1.3tn survey could also be too low, because hedge funds and other managers running risk-premium strategies do not report to it, so the true size is uncertain in both directions.

added_claims.speaker: Nick Balters
added_claims.quote: nobody suddenly thought that systematic is the way but systematic is the pay to deliver into an index format what otherwise could be a cumbersome and tedious process
added_claims.claim: QIS grew not because clients suddenly believed in systematic investing but because an index or swap wrapper delivers a rules-based exposure with less operational burden and better cash efficiency than building it in-house.

added_claims.speaker: Nick Balters
added_claims.quote: there's a lot of governance around this business. Um some others would be using external calculation agents
added_claims.claim: QIS indices are run under governance: European benchmark rules require an independent calculation agent, and banks use either an internally separated calculation unit or an external agent, a business choice as long as governance holds.

added_claims.speaker: Nick Balters
added_claims.quote: Generally we build we build product for scale because that in itself is associated with how we can see the profitability of this business
added_claims.claim: Because QIS profitability depends on scale, popular bank trend/CTA indices cover only the deepest liquid markets (the host notes they omit smaller markets); broader indices with illiquid assets exist but support only a fraction of the capacity.
added_claims.testable: partly - capacity estimates need market-impact data

added_claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds

added_claims.claim: Many 'new' risk-premium indices pitched to a quant desk are small twists on existing strategies, a sign of pressure to launch products for their own sake and of over-optimisation.

added_claims.speaker: Nick Balters
added_claims.quote: I think crowding implications have been overstated because they haven't necessarily been looked through the economics and the mechanics of the strategies
added_claims.claim: Crowding concerns about QIS are generally overstated because they are not analysed strategy by strategy (liquidity-allocation premia, risk-sharing premia and behavioural strategies each react differently), but that does not mean there is no problem.

added_claims.testable: partly - premium decay can be tested by strategy type

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the point that vol-targeting a strategy that recovers after volatility spikes works against it is Nick Balters', in his answer; the host only asked about vol targeting.
corrections.fix: Nick Balters: volatility targeting a strategy that is meant to recover after a volatility spike works against its ability to recover and yields a sub-optimal profile, so making a QIS option-friendly through vol control has a cost.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: Nick Balters makes the argument (trend following may benefit from early crowding; the problem is risk management of negative skew events); Morris only interjects 'to the fire'.
corrections.fix: Nick Balters: behavioural strategies such as trend following may benefit from early crowding; the real issue is moderating negative-skew events (risk management), not premium erosion.

corrections.issue: Nick calls the $600bn (+/-$100bn) broker-dealer figure a rough guess ('I'm just making it up really'), and the 2018 and 2021 'winter periods' were setbacks in the growth, not periods of growth.
corrections.fix: Nick's rough guess is that broker-dealer QIS is close to $600bn plus or minus $100bn (no hard data); the business has grown over the years with a few setback ('winter') periods, around 2018 and 2021.

completeness_estimate: 0.88 - the first reader got the QIS size, client, wrapper, data-mining, congestion and crowding arguments; missed the SG short-term traders YTD data, currency attribution, why fixed income/FX are small, survey undercount, the packaging rationale, calculation-agent governance, scale-versus-capacity incentive, new-product-twist observation and the 'crowding overstated' conclusion; two speaker misattributions and one overstated figure.
